export function createDragState(){let active=false;let id=null;let x=0;const finite=(v)=>typeof v==="number"&&Number.isFinite(v);const matching=(e)=>Boolean(active&&e&&e.pointerId===id);return{down(e){if(active)return;if(!e||!finite(e.clientX))return;active=true;id=e.pointerId;x=e.clientX},move(e){if(!matching(e)||!finite(e.clientX))return;x=e.clientX},up(e){if(!matching(e))return;active=false;id=null},cancel(e){if(!matching(e))return;active=false;id=null},blur(){active=false;id=null},snapshot(){return{active,id,x}}}}
Reasoning: down is gated by active so a second pointer cannot start or overwrite a drag. move, up, and cancel accept only the captured pointerId, so foreign pointers cannot move, end, or cancel the drag. blur clears only drag lifecycle state. Nonfinite clientX is rejected before mutation, so prior x remains intact. Ambiguity: up and cancel do not require finite clientX because they are lifecycle actions, not coordinate commits; x is intentionally retained after up, cancel, or blur until the next accepted down or move.
